title: synthetic-oncall-health-prober-and-quiet-hours-manager
author: Ravi Shah
release_notes: Add a scheduled synthetic on-call health prober and configurable quiet-hours manager that reduces noisy alerts and introduces a compact daily digest for on-call. Rollout: opt-in by default for small teams; global flag for enterprise tenants.
description: Motivation: On-call teams receive a large fraction of noisy or transient alerts during low-activity windows. This PR introduces a small, opinionated subsystem to proactively run lightweight synthetic checks against known critical callpaths and to manage 'quiet windows' that suppress non-actionable alerts while surfacing a condensed digest to responders. The change pairs two components: (1) a Synthetic Health Prober that executes short, deterministic probes (HTTP, DB ping, RPC smoke) and attaches contextual telemetry to the incident-bot's ephemeral snapshot store; (2) a Quiet Hours Manager that enforces configurable suppression policies and orchestrates an end-of-window digest that summarizes failing probes, recent flaps, and recommended runbook snippets. The description below captures the contents, design decisions, and rollout plan. Checklist: [x] unit tests for probe scheduler and suppression rules; [x] e2e harness for quiet-window lifecycle; [x] lightweight UI card for on-call digest in Slack; [x] documentation and example config in docs/quiet-windows.md. Design notes: probes are pluggable via a Probe interface (http_ping, tcp_connect, redis_smoke, rpc_smoke). Each probe runs with strict timeouts and circuit-breaker behavior; failures are annotated with recent traces and a short hypothesis string (e.g. "DNS timeout on regional egress"). Quiet windows are configured per-service and per-oncall-rotation; default behavior is to suppress alerts with severity < P1 and history of >50% transient flips in the last 15m. Digest generation uses prefix sampling of KV snapshots to avoid exposing full logs. Security: probe payloads are synthetic and do not access customer PII; credentials for internal checks are pulled from the existing secrets backend with read-only tokens. Rollout: feature gate off by default for accounts; enable for a pilot beta on the 'platform-sre' Linear team (ENG-2049). Links: design doc: https://linear.app/ENG-2049/notes/synthetic-prober-quiet-windows; runbook templates: ./runbooks/quiet-window-suggestions.md.

review_thread: Aisha Kumar: Please ensure the probe scheduler never runs >2 concurrent probes per service during quiet windows; resource contention caused flakiness in earlier experiments.
Ravi Shah: Updated scheduler to use per-service token bucket and added E2E that asserts concurrency <=2.
Mateo Ruiz: Can we avoid storing raw traces in the digest? We should only attach short trace ids and an indexed pointer into the ephemeral snapshot store.
Ravi Shah: Accepted; digest now contains trace ids and a 120-char contextual blurb. Full snapshots are available via the snapshot link with RBAC enforcement.
Eve Chen: Lint flagged magic numbers in suppressor.go; prefer constants and comments referencing the design doc.
Ravi Shah: Addressed; moved to named constants and added comments + link to design note.
Aisha Kumar: Approving once minor comment on backoff policy is addressed.
Ravi Shah: Adjusted backoff to exponential capped at 2m; added unit test that simulates repeated flaps.
Aisha Kumar: Approved. Mateo Ruiz: Approved. Eve Chen: Approved.
